rationale: Evidence from iteration 3 (kd 0.4, ki 0.5, base_speed 1.2, kp 1.5, sensors at x = ±0.05, score 342.03): the oval now finishes 16 of 20 runs with progress 0.97 and max_error 0.043, down from about 0.061. That confirms derivative damping was the lever on the oval. The s-bend and slalom still end off track with progress 0.28 and 0.19. Their line_loss_events are 0.55 and 1.0 per run, and max_error is about 0.062 to 0.064, so the robot loses the tape on tight bends and then drifts past the 0.06 m limit. Steering_oscillation is 0.20 to 0.28, which is acceptable and not the failure. ki has had no measurable effect in any iteration, so I keep it at 0.5 to isolate the geometry change. The remaining problem is sensor coverage: the outer sensors at ±0.05 lose the tape when the robot is tilted or offset on sharp bends. Change: widen the sensor array to x = -0.07, -0.035, 0, 0.035, 0.07 (outer sensors at ±0.07, within the ±0.08 limit). Every other field is unchanged, so the effect of the wider footprint is isolated. Expected result: fewer line-loss events on the s-bend and slalom (ideally below 0.3 and below 0.5), progress above 0.4 on those tracks, and max_error below 0.06. The oval should hold near 0.04 to 0.05 max_error. Risk: wider spacing gives the robot less precise centring on straights, which could raise oval oscillation, so I will watch oval steering_oscillation (currently 0.28). Hypotheses: (a) sensor spread, not controller gain, limits s-bend and slalom; (b) if line_loss stays at 1 per run with the wider array, the line is lost at the bend entry and the next test is sensor_size 0.016 or a sensor shift forward to y = 0.07. Next measurements: per-track progress, line_loss_events, max_error, steering_oscillation, and distance before the first off-track event.
